mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in each of the last three weeks (-32.9 -> -30.0 -> -29.1 -> -26.7), showing persistent positive momentum; this autocorrelated recovery trend is expected to continue over the next four weeks absent a shock.
failure_condition: If the mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days despite the prior monotonic rise, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Falling RESIDENTIAL mobility (11.9 -> 11.1 -> 11.3 -> 10.6) indicates households are spending less time at home and are more willing to travel for shopping and leisure; once RESIDENTIAL drops below a behavioral threshold, RETAIL_REC should rise within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10.5 for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 11.9 to 10.6 over 3 weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls below 10.5 but the mean of RETAIL_REC over the following 2 weeks does not increase relative to the prior 2 weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility reflect restored commuting patterns that generate incidental retail visits near transit hubs and office districts, producing a compounded lift in RETAIL_REC beyond what either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise week-on-week simultaneously for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -21.1 to -18.7 and TRANSIT rose from -33.9 to -30.6 over the same period
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise concurrently for 2 weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the following 2-4 weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under an easing-restrictions regime, a sharp jump in PARKS mobility without a parallel acceleration in RETAIL_REC indicates substitution of outdoor leisure for shopping and recreation trips, which suppresses RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week while RETAIL_REC growth stalls below 1 point
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -23.3 to -13.4 while RETAIL_REC gains slowed between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS surges more than 5 points in a week but RETAIL_REC still increases over the following 4 weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A seasonal upswing in outdoor activity, reflected in rising PARKS mobility, correlates with a broader willingness to leave home that also boosts retail footfall in the immediate following week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -23.3 to -13.4 across the snapshot period
failure_condition: If PARKS continues rising but the mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days decreases relative to the prior week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden sharp drop in TRANSIT mobility beyond a critical threshold signals renewed public caution or avoidance behavior (e.g., crowding fears), which typically precedes a pullback in retail visits within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has ranged between -33.9 and -30.6 without breaching -35
failure_condition: If TRANSIT drops below -35 in a given week but RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Coordinated increases in GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES mobility reflect loosened policy restrictions on essential and work-related movement, jointly signaling a broader reopening that extends into retail and recreation activity over the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both increase for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 0.9 to 3.7 and WORKPLACES rose from -21.1 to -18.7 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both rise concurrently for 2 weeks but the mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime where TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed despite recovery in other categories, limited transit capacity constrains physical access to retail destinations, capping or reversing RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30 for 3 or more consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has stayed below -30 for all four observed weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -30 for 3+ weeks yet RETAIL_REC still rises over the following 2 weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.
